findings.observation: Spend requires the full prefix and rejects ancestors ≥128; epoch !=1 returns HandoverRequired. This is an issuer log limit, not only UI. crates/postage-spend/src/lib.rs:123–156,191–239; crates/finalizer/src/engine/guard.rs:15–73
findings.impact: After 128 records or an epoch change, new paid operations stop while funds still exist.
findings.action: Durable indexed spent set, bounded authenticated snapshots, state transfer/handover without resetting nullifiers; a regression significantly longer than 128.
findings.simplification: Keep one issuer-global journal; do not introduce new sharded committees now.
findings.tradeoff: A targeted lifecycle rework is required; simply raising the constant keeps O(N) ancestry and does not solve epochs.
findings.progress: Indexed finalized history removes the old 128-entry lifetime fence without resetting issuer spent keys. Accepted native evidence covers 144 funded spends, original SpendRecord recovery, explicit same-epoch renewal with 18 spends / 216 signature checks, and authentic terminal closing. The daemon now bootstraps original closing lineage and cumulative spent history through bounded ordinary-peer pages before successor signer activation. The accepted multi-epoch native gate proves 133 spends, two closings and 1605 independently checked signatures across three genuinely selected committees, including incomplete old validators, a fresh successor, SQL rollback, role revocation, cold resume and an expired nonsigning archive serving all 130 old records. Separate hostile ingress evidence proves wrong-target closing, altered original QC and mixed canonical history pages cannot alter SQL state or start a signer; exact originals recover after crash. This supersedes earlier library-only and running-native status. Automatic authority acquisition/renewal, closure after old-authority outage and recovery of pending inputs remain required. AR-R01 and full V1 remain open.

findings.classification: R02 / P0 / confirmed limit and calculation
findings.observation: Public sender active queue ≤128, terminal retirement not found; the scheduler processes one entry from the shared list every 500 ms. crates/core/src/public_sender.rs:12–18,225–359; crates/node/src/public_sender.rs:86–121,130–135
findings.impact: The 129th sponsored send is rejected; with 128 jobs the queue yields ≥64 s between scheduled passes over one job, not counting work.
findings.action: Persistent stages, terminal retirement, correct distinction of reserved/spent/refundable, a bounded ready queue, and event-driven scheduling.
findings.simplification: One job ledger and one scheduler instead of the active JSON plus temporary Work/views.
findings.tradeoff: Do not reset a reservation after QC as unused; keep the bounded active queue but not a lifetime cap.
findings.progress: Candidate 5 passes the funded 128-job / 127-paused scheduling gate and the complete two-message sender workflow: original allocations survive crash, six independently verified QC signatures and twenty genuine receipts establish actual finality/storage, a wrong-Noise copied offer is refused, SQL-fault retry succeeds, and the offline recipient recovers both originals after cache loss. The same binary passes TCP/QUIC custody invalidation and hostile multi-epoch history ingress. Targeted regression passes 46 Core wallet/preparation tests (30 sender), 96 daemon library tests and node Clippy; 59 frontend tests, 19 model tests, fmt and TypeScript/Vite completed before the user narrowed intermediate checks. The workspace run was interrupted and the full suite is deferred to the end of the complete plan. Successful terminal retirement and a durable stage ledger remain open; the prior common-holder obstacle is now removed by durable signed history with accepted ordinary disjoint-book recovery. Successful jobs still occupy the active queue; retirement and durable status require end-to-end completion.

findings.classification: R03 / P0 / confirmed logic + missing integration
findings.observation: Ordinary signed history now restores both exact originals across genuinely disjoint funded data/index rosters, after sender disappearance and actual provider loss. Native compatibility and final targeted checks share one immutable application input set.
findings.impact: The declared two-book range now survives original-roster disjointness and loss. Completeness across actual MLS control/epochs and beyond the finite manifest, first Welcome, successful retirement and independent repair remain unproved.
findings.action: Finish whole ordinary user sending and retirement; then close first Welcome, actual MLS epoch/gap recovery and autonomous data/index repair.
findings.simplification: One logical index and a shared physical custody store; do not create a second economic spend for it.
findings.tradeoff: A separate discovery location is required; dropping it without a replacement loses history. The new model already provides a bounded index entitlement within the same spend.
findings.progress: Accepted the complete declared two-original range across two genuinely funded books whose original ten-data and ten-index rosters are both disjoint. All 24 candidate books were paid before the genuine beacon across 60 active bonded operators. Ordinary sends span a cold sender and 3600/900-second leases; the older live original remains the anchor. Recipient recovers both exact originals without sender after actual data/index loss, missing public trust, two SQL import failures, partial progress and cold/cache-loss dedup. The same source/binary passes existing two-concurrent-message one-book compatibility and 94 backend /21 frontend, Clippy/fmt, 614 unchanged inputs. All failed runs and the finite pre-beacon fixture failure remain recorded. This proves the declared finite range in one MLS epoch; arbitrary history/epochs, Welcome, successful sender retirement and autonomous R10 remain open.
findings.recipient_next: Complete ordinary user sending end-to-end: wallet/price/TTL/budget, one truthful status for UI/CLI/MCP and successful sender retirement preserving durable originals/history. Current UI has no ordinary wallet/policy selection; successful jobs still occupy the active queue. Add only work needed for an observed obstacle to that scenario. Then close offline first Welcome, actual MLS epochs/gaps and autonomous R10. Keep 67 cards/22 E2E/three platforms and no push.
findings.recipient_core_progress: Accepted local Core one-descriptor traversal: read-only discovery, opaque 120-second local fetch token, exact ciphertext binding and shared atomic message/MLS/dedup/bookmark commit. Current incoming epoch/index, saved revision, strictly advancing sequence and retention remain checked, including empty old tokens. Seven independently reviewed tests, compilation RED before production; affected gate 22 backend/21 frontend, production Clippy/fmt and 587 matching inputs. This was the local prerequisite; subsequent native integration is recorded separately in recipient_runtime_evidence.
findings.history_manifest_progress: Accepted crypto prerequisite for a finite signed directory: 1–128 exact descriptor references, 1–4 distinct candidate index keys each, 32 KiB bound, longest-lived exact paid-descriptor anchor, original per-reference expiry, deferred exact descriptor matching and direction/epoch/revision checkpoint fences. Candidate keys do not prove paid placement. Persistence, native manifest transport/publication/retrieval, completeness and MLS control history are not claimed.
findings.history_storage_progress: Accepted local paid-anchor manifest persistence/read: full historical Core trust and original operator binding, unchanged funding/QC/receipt, shared SQLCipher index state/clock and quota, exact retry, cold revision fences, preservation of live descriptor references, expired pruning, target-bound whole-manifest reads and corruption rejection. findings.history_core_progress: Accepted local exact outgoing manifests and durable incoming checkpoints, including cross-anchor revision/issuance fences, live-reference preservation, cold signature verification, expired checkpoint retention, exact retries with a shorter expired reference, actual INSERT/UPDATE rollback, and unchanged message/MLS/outbox/fetch progress. Seven independently reviewed tests; current-input compile RED before production. Affected gate 91 backend/21 frontend, production Clippy/fmt and 597 unchanged inputs. Earlier epoch rows remain retained; no control/Welcome catch-up or complete-history claim. Native path still uses index intersection.

Core requires committed outgoing history/current incoming scope, rejects downgrade/rollback/equivocation, and binds fetched directories to the current live pointer before atomic history acceptance. Saved outgoing plaintext reopens signed records; incoming plaintext rechecks checkpoint hash. Seven independently reviewed tests, current-input compile RED: 11 crypto /21 Core before production; affected gate: 107 backend /21 frontend, Clippy/fmt and 602 unchanged inputs. Ordinary multi-book manifest transport and reference-bound message import remain unintegrated.
findings.history_pointer_compatibility_progress: Six existing real-node legacy mailbox regressions pass on the same 602 input fingerprints: cold sender-absent lookup/cache loss, forged DHT refusal, background routing slots and bounded request/job work. Actual node binary hash is retained. This is compatibility evidence, not v2 manifest network acceptance.

Concurrent distinct fetches merge without skipping earlier gaps; exact retry performs no SQL write. Eight independently reviewed tests, REVISE to ACCEPT before production and accepted-input missing-API compile RED. Affected gate: 57 backend/21 frontend, Clippy/fmt, 604 unchanged inputs. Native manifest put/read, ordinary multi-book integration and full AR-R03 remain open; runtime still intersects index rosters.

Full portable payload budget and read-clock commit precede release; original funding/QC/receipt are unchanged. Three store tests prove nonfirst-anchor lookup, historical trust, exact size, SQL rollback and scope/expiry. Real native gate proves paid funding and three QC signatures, exact signed history/anchor, cold index with sender daemon absent, SQL put/update/read failures and same-anchor revision rollback. Recipient authenticates the exact pointer-bound directory and retrieves each pending reference from its own signed index candidates through genuine paid-index/holder verification, then atomically imports original message/MLS/dedup/per-operation progress. Three native gates pass on one binary: sender four SQL-fault stages/cold retries/all-ten independent remote audit; recipient actual loss, different surviving indexes/holders, missing trust, both exact-message SQL failures, partial progress/cold retry/dedup; legacy direct retrieval/copies/inspection. findings.observation: Copies/inspection are real, but copy is owner-initiated; there is no autonomous R10 chain. crates/node/src/custody_copy.rs:76–115; spec/paid-custody-copies-v1.md; D05-paid-index-store/NEXT.md
findings.impact: After losing 3 of 10 copies, the copy count does not recover by itself while clients are offline.
findings.action: Operator anti-entropy, actual ciphertext checks, replacement authorization, quotas/budget, a durable repair queue, and location/index updates.
findings.simplification: One bounded repair scheduler serves data and index; no separate global repair consensus.
findings.tradeoff: A live source, spare capacity, permissions/funds, and TTL are needed. During a partition, temporary bounded over-replication is safer than deletion on suspicion.

findings.observation: The first MLS Welcome is created in add_contact and the direct outbox, but not as a public durable sender job. crates/core/src/lib.rs:358–433; crates/node/src/custody_sync.rs:125–128
findings.impact: A new recipient without the Welcome cannot use the exporter/decrypt stored application messages after the sender disappears.
findings.action: Durable private rendezvous/control delivery before an established conversation; an offline first-contact test.
findings.simplification: A shared reliable encrypted-object pipeline with a separate control type, not another centralized inbox.
findings.tradeoff: Separate initial capability/retention rules are needed; the existing established-chat E2E does not prove this case.
findings.current_implementation: Still open: initial Welcome is in durable direct outbox; public sender excludes it. Cold recipient needs a pre-conversation capability/read path and atomic control completion. Established-conversation history gates do not prove this flow.

findings.observation: Network ciphertext recovery does not restore lost root/MLS state; there is no full backup/import/anti-rollback. crates/store/src/lib.rs:95–161; crates/crypto/src/lib.rs:104–113,449–493; backlog [I06]; apps/desktop/src/
findings.impact: Losing the last local profile can leave data that is available on the network but undecryptable.
findings.action: A consistent encrypted backup/import or device rejoin with an explicitly bounded old history; do not roll back spent/ownership/revocations.
findings.simplification: One consistent export format/version for the entire secret and transactional part of the profile.
findings.tradeoff: The key recovery guarantee must be explicitly defined; copying a single DB without lifecycle/keyring is not enough.

findings.classification: R07 / P1 / trust boundary and missing proof
findings.observation: Trusted-attestors-v1 accepts a threshold checkpoint instead of independently establishing L2 canonical finality. Keys/processes do not prove independence. spec/postage/trusted-checkpoints.md:1–66; crates/core/src/checkpoints.rs; contracts/src/NodeRegistry.sol:4–7
findings.impact: A compromised threshold can legitimize a false root; quorum disappearance halts new operations after the lease.
findings.action: An explicit testnet trust manifest, independent operators/distribution, a company-off cold join, and outage/handover E2E.
findings.simplification: Keep explicitly federated checkpoints for V1 instead of a new light client; do not call them trustless.
findings.tradeoff: Operation is simpler, but the trust threshold remains. A stronger guarantee requires a separate finality verification project.

findings.observation: Funding/spend/custody receipts exist; SubsidyVault, royalty, and full operator settlement were not found. contracts/src/PostageIssuer.sol:4–7,103–123; contracts/src/; backlog [L03–L05]
findings.impact: The postage stamp is spent, but the economic incentive for long-term storage/repair is not closed. Not the same as lost funds in a running mainnet: the target is still testnet.
findings.action: Finish bounded resource compensation/reserve, or separately approve a volunteer-funded preview without promising a self-sustaining network.
findings.simplification: For the preview — transparent sponsored quotas; defer payouts only by owner decision.
findings.tradeoff: The autonomy of economic operation changes; a token funding proof must not be passed off as a paid storage service.

findings.classification: R09 / P1 / confirmed UI model mismatch
findings.observation: Core delivery_status returns queued/delivered, replicas=0,target=10; the public sender keeps a different Work.view. crates/core/src/lib.rs:831–841; apps/desktop/src/DeliveryBadge.tsx; crates/node/src/public_sender.rs:397–410
findings.impact: The user does not see the actual durable state and may confuse a recipient ACK with a fulfilled retention promise.
findings.action: One persisted read model with independent delivery/durability/funding states for UI/CLI/MCP.
findings.simplification: Two or three orthogonal statuses instead of a linear ladder that blocks a quick DM waiting for ten copies.
findings.tradeoff: A projection migration is needed; delivered should not be renamed to read, and a receipt should not be counted as future availability.

findings.classification: R10 / P1 / user entry points not finished
findings.observation: MCP exists; CLI identity/send/delivery/poll/ack and a shipped skill are missing. The wallet backend is not reachable through ordinary purchase/sponsor UI. crates/node/src/main.rs; crates/node/src/bin/agentic-mcp.rs; apps/desktop/src/desktop-api.ts; src-tauri/capabilities/main.json
findings.impact: Preparing paid messaging requires owner IPC/manual orchestration; the user/agent does not get the declared ready interface.
findings.action: A thin CLI over the same typed daemon service; wallet/price/TTL/budget UX without manual internal commands.
findings.simplification: Not a new agent service, and not a CLI calling MCP as a mandatory dependency.
findings.tradeoff: The shared policy is preserved; extra adapters are small compared with a new protocol subsystem.

findings.classification: R11 / P1 / confirmed extra build dependency
findings.observation: The default desktop build unconditionally launches the ZK build/prover and packages sidecars, although the new public path uses no ZK. scripts/build-desktop.mjs:15–21; crates/postage-zk/build.rs:1–29; crates/postage-spend/Cargo.toml; tauri.bundle.conf
findings.impact: Clean builds, toolchain size, and platform support depend on the unused new sender path.
findings.action: Isolate legacy verify/prove, frozen guest/image ID, and compatible readers; move native public types out of the shared proof dependency.
findings.simplification: An ordinary V1 target without the prover; a separate legacy regression target.
findings.tradeoff: Access to old obligations must not be lost, and a private/public ticket must not gain a second right to one funding; migration requires fixture checks.

findings.observation: Node/MCP use Unix IPC; non-Unix main explicitly reports Windows pipe support is pending; desktop-host imports unix IPC. crates/node/src/lib.rs:2–9; crates/node/src/main.rs:106–155; crates/node/src/bin/agentic-mcp.rs:15–18; crates/desktop-host/src/lib.rs:2,78
findings.impact: Windows x86_64 from the mandatory scope is not currently a working application.
findings.action: A thin IPC transport adapter: Unix sockets/Windows named pipes, equivalent ACLs, shutdown/cancellation, and tests.
findings.simplification: Keep one Core; do not move the product to an HTTP service for the platform's sake.
findings.tradeoff: Native CI and packaging will be needed. A Mac ad-hoc app and a Linux container do not replace the three installer gates.

findings.classification: R13 / P1 / confirmed structure; effect not measured
findings.observation: Synchronous Core/crypto/SQL run inside the runtime select; MLS prepare restores and serializes the provider entirely. crates/node/src/runtime.rs:372–394,645–700; crates/crypto/src/lib.rs:104–113,449–493
findings.impact: Profile growth/expensive proofs can increase event-loop stalls, UI/network latency, and retry storms.
findings.action: An incremental transactional provider, a bounded worker pool for immutable verification, and Core recheck+CAS before commit.
findings.simplification: One writer and structured completion events, not many independently mutating Cores.
findings.tradeoff: A benchmark is needed to assess the gain; specific milliseconds must not be claimed without measurement.
findings.confidence: high for structure; medium for effect size

findings.observation: The index is entirely JSON/BTreeMap, load rechecks every record, read persists state; max objects ≤128/max bytes ≤8 MiB. Two full portable test objects >256 KiB. crates/postage-spend/src/custody/index/storage.rs:15–21,52–113,272–306; custody.rs:29–44; tests/paid_index.rs:600–603
findings.impact: The index is not ready for a long history; the compact descriptor accumulates expensive evidence, and read triggers a write.
findings.action: SQL rows/indexes + deduplicated authenticated proof bundles, page bounds, and retention; cache verified immutable evidence.
findings.simplification: One proof object by content hash per book/authority/QC instead of full duplication in every record.
findings.tradeoff: Hash-only without availability of the original proof will worsen cold verification. Fixture size does not equal the production mean.

findings.observation: The JobsPanel/button and jobs MCP methods are still active although orders are V2. apps/desktop/src/ChatShell.tsx:65–78; apps/desktop/src/JobsPanel.tsx; crates/node/src/mcp.rs:187–195; crates/core/src/jobs.rs
findings.impact: Extra UI/security/regression surface and team attention.
findings.action: An optional v2-jobs feature/tool capability; remove from the default UI/catalog, keep historical readers/tests.
findings.simplification: Isolate; do not delete all working modules and do not continue V2 development.
findings.tradeoff: Do not confuse node/postage_jobs.rs (legacy proof work) and service_discovery (operators) with V2 orders.

findings.classification: R16 / P2 / confirmed coupling; not a Cargo cycle
findings.observation: Core depends on finalizer/L2/proof, postage-spend depends on Core; desktop-host pulls in node for IPC. Cargo.toml of all crates; dependency-audit.json
findings.impact: Economic policy/native host are tied to the heavy graph; a payment change affects Core and the desktop build.
findings.action: Extract a small neutral IPC/API and verified funding/authority types; policy adapters around the transactional Core.
findings.simplification: Keep the current workspace, merge duplicated state/DTOs; no global reorganization.
findings.tradeoff: A targeted type migration is cheaper than a rewrite. No real Cargo dependency cycles were found.

findings.observation: The runtime signing_seed is materialized in a 0600 file inside a 0700 directory; this protects against other UIDs, not against arbitrary code of the same user. crates/node/src/mcp.rs:381–431
findings.impact: An agent with unrestricted same-UID filesystem access can read neighboring runtime credentials; MCP restrictions alone do not isolate it.
findings.action: Declare a trusted same-UID boundary, or run untrusted runtimes in an OS sandbox/separate UID with one delegated handle.
findings.simplification: For V1, limit the supported agent host model; do not build a universal VM manager of our own.
findings.tradeoff: The simplification is acceptable only with an explicit absence of a sandbox guarantee for arbitrary coding agents; the API grants themselves are correct.

findings.classification: R18 / P1 / mandatory product not integrated
findings.observation: MLS add/remove and the generic consensus exist, but not full groups/roles/devices/control delivery. crates/crypto/src/lib.rs:211–229; crates/core/src/lib.rs:863–879; apps/desktop/src/; backlog [G01–G06]
findings.impact: Groups cannot be considered closed by the library; the key messenger capability now lags behind the economics primitives.
findings.action: One user group vertical: authorized encrypted control, control payload availability before finalize, deterministic reject/no-op, UI.
findings.simplification: Reuse the generic ordering only for membership control, not for every application message.
findings.tradeoff: Replacing it with a single online group sequencer would simplify but change decentralization/fault tolerance; I do not recommend doing so silently.

findings.observation: MLS past epochs=3 and a bounded sender ratchet; long offline recovery is not linked to the control/application history read order. crates/crypto/src/lib.rs:140–145,253; spec/mls-adapter-v1.md
findings.impact: If all epochs are applied first and old keys are deleted, later ciphertexts may become undecryptable.
findings.action: Epoch-aware catch-up that processes the relevant messages before GC, or a safe rejoin/explicit gap; tests beyond the window.
findings.simplification: Do not keep all epochs indefinitely just for recovery.
findings.tradeoff: Unbounded key retention changes forward secrecy and resources; the value 3 itself is not a discovered crypto flaw.
findings.confidence: medium: the limit is confirmed, a whole failing E2E was not run

findings.observation: Store authenticates the DB and uses FULL/WAL/transactions; the v1 schema with CREATE IF NOT EXISTS is not a complete migration system. crates/store/src/lib.rs:95–161; scripts/build-desktop.mjs; core tests/profile tests
findings.impact: An application upgrade or restoring an old backup can break state compatibility/roll back local fences without an explicit policy.
findings.action: Versioned forward migrations, backup/rollback during migration, compatible readers, and anti-rollback of external authorities; kill/disk-full tests.
findings.simplification: One persisted schema version and an explicit compatibility envelope, not a separate migration system for every JSON namespace.
findings.tradeoff: Stricter format discipline; silent reset is forbidden. A wrong key is already fail-closed — this must be preserved.

findings.observation: Public funding commitment/signature/ticket identity are bound to issuer/operation/resources; formats are strictly recognized; the global spent namespace is shared. crates/core/src/public_postage.rs:67–159,193–201; crates/postage-spend/src/verification.rs:72–103; spec/postage/public-signed-postage-v1.md
findings.impact: No obvious double-spend bypass via an operation change or a malformed public→ZK fallback was found.
findings.action: Keep domain separation/strict parser/the same spent set; separate cross-format migration vectors.
findings.simplification: A public signature is a reasonable simplification instead of new ZK anonymity.
findings.tradeoff: This is not a formal crypto audit; payment, book, and metadata are linkable; E2EE content is preserved.

findings.observation: Core/store bind message/crypto/outbox/operations/CAS in one transaction; the incoming ACK and index receipt are issued after commit. crates/store/src/lib.rs:229–329; crates/core/src/lib.rs:653–706; index/storage.rs:269–270,305; tests/paid_index.rs:562–630
findings.impact: An SQL failure does not become a successful storage/delivery promise; a scoped retry does not create a second record.
findings.action: Do not break this boundary during performance refactors; keep fault injection on real SQL.
findings.simplification: A shared command service instead of three implementations of the UI/CLI/MCP rules.
findings.tradeoff: Consensus/receipt are correct within their meaning; a commit does not prove future availability or history completeness.

findings.observation: The latest D05 gate is 270 backend tests; the 791 workspace and 7 native scenarios refer to the previous sender. evidence/reviews/D05-paid-index-store/{checks.json,release.json,README.md}; evidence/reviews/P02-public-sender-daemon/{final-checks.json,native-checks.json}
findings.impact: The sum of green reports creates a false impression of the current application's readiness; module acceptance is already correct.
findings.action: A current-revision manifest: workspace/live/native/OS gates separately; do not delete failed/rejected runs.
findings.simplification: A short default V1 gate + independent targeted heavy/legacy gates; the final release gate is shared.
findings.tradeoff: An up-to-date CI environment is needed; my limited Python checks do not replace a Rust/EVM/native rerun.

findings.observation: After moving jobs aside, 8 provider cards, subsidy/royalty/settlement, two group privacy profiles, three OSes, and recovery are still mandatory. release-scope.json; backlog [O01–O08,L03–L05,G05,U06]
findings.impact: The nearest release contains several products at once while the simple paid offline DM lacks a complete lifecycle.
findings.action: Propose to the owner a separate narrow preview scope, reducing provider diversity/economic onboarding first of all.
findings.simplification: Key-only identity + paid/sponsored testnet books; keep P2P, E2EE, R10, offline/history/backup, and the shared agent interfaces.
findings.tradeoff: Losing free Google/Telegram/org onboarding and economic self-sufficiency must be explicitly approved; the current 67/22 cannot be considered closed under the new boundary.
findings.confidence: high for scope breadth; medium for product priority

full_native_fourth_attempt.reason: Source inspection found recipient lacked the old public checkpoint needed to serve a renewal suffix. Genuine live public anchor setup was added without postage/history/configuration state, independently ACCEPTED.

full_native_fifth_attempt.failure: Timed out importing old records from the expired original archive; cause not established.
